thread:
sarah: Quick heads-up — after the tool-call changes landed yesterday we're seeing a regression in decode batching for chat flows that do function/tool calls. p95 generation latency up ~30% on some workloads. Anyone else see this?

jamie: Saw it in the canary. Repro steps: multi-turn chat with structured tool output. When decoder hits a tool-call stop token it pauses, we resume after tool result, and batch formation drops.

noah: Yep. Profiler shows a lot more small batches and KV cache misses around the pause boundary. Dump from last run: 
```
PerfSummary:
  before: tokens/sec=48k, p50=120ms, p95=310ms
  after:  tokens/sec=34k, p50=160ms, p95=410ms
BatchStats:
  avg_batch_size: before=12 -> after=6
  small_batches(<3): before=4% -> after=21%
KVCache:
  reuse_rate: before=94% -> after=78%
```

jamie: That avg_batch_size drop is the root cause. The queue policy currently flushes on stop-token hits immediately. That makes sense for correctness but hurts throughput.

sarah: We need a heuristic: allow a short pause-window after a stop-token to collect more decodes that will resume quickly. But mustn't delay tool execution for long. Ideas? token-budget targets? max wait ms?

noah: Proposal A: pause-window of 20ms after a stop-token; if no more tokens enqueued, flush. Also use token-budget target for batch formation: aim for ~10 tokens per request before dispatch, but cap wall time to 40ms. This should reduce tiny batches without impacting perceived tool latency.

jamie: Proposal B: classify requests as "tool-call heavy" vs "no-tools" at request arrival. Keep separate queues and batching policies. Tool-heavy queue uses conservative pause-window but has priority when tool result is ready. No-tools queue batches aggressively. Advantage: avoids penalties for regular streams.

infra-bot: Canary deployed: feature/decoding-pause-window @ canary cluster at 1710610000. Metrics ingestion enabled.

sarah: Related KV issue — when we pause and the model instance frees the KV slab to serve other batches, the resumed decode ends up with a cache miss and recompute. We should pin KV for paused contexts or serialize small resumed decodes on the same worker. Thoughts?

noah: Two options: (1) lightweight pin: keep KV in LRU with short TTL (100-200ms) for paused contexts; (2) resume-on-same-worker: add sticky routing for resumed sessions for a short window. (1) is memory-friendly but still allows eviction; (2) simpler correctness but can reduce scheduling flexibility.

jamie: Also kernel selection matters: currently we re-evaluate kernels on resume and sometimes pick a slower kernel because sequence-length profile changed. We should keep the kernel decision sticky per session for a short time-span so pauses don't flip kernels mid-request.

sarah: Agreed. For experiments let's try: pause-window=20ms, token_budget=10, max_wait=40ms, KV_TTL=150ms, sticky-kernel=true. We'll run microbench across 3 payload patterns: heavy-tool (40% tool turns), light-tool (10%), no-tool baseline.

noah: I'll add perf harness and compare baseline vs new heuristic. Quick command I'll run: 
```
./perf_harness --profile decode_pause --run-sets heavy-tool,light-tool,baseline --iters 500
```

jamie: If results look good we can A/B the change behind a flag. Also need to update observability: add breakouts for resumed-decode latency and KV reuse rate in the model dashboard.

sarah: Action items: @noah run microbench and paste numbers here; @jamie wire dashboard panels; I'll draft RFC for pause-window + queue split and include rollback criteria (tokens/sec drop >5% or p95 increase >10%).

infra-bot: noah started run decode_pause at 1710610300.

noah: Quick initial numbers from run1 (heavy-tool): 
```
baseline: tokens/sec=35.2k, p95=420ms, avg_batch_size=6
heuristic-v1: tokens/sec=41.1k, p95=360ms, avg_batch_size=10
KV_reuse: baseline=76% -> v1=88%
```

jamie: Nice improvement. Can you dump a trace where we still see small batches? That will help tune token_budget vs max_wait.

noah: Will do. One caveat: structured outputs that include long stop-token sequences (e.g., tools which emit JSON close markers) create many short pauses. We might need special-case: if stop-token pattern is multi-token, treat as a stronger signal to flush immediately.

sarah: Good call. Add rule: multi-token stop sequences => immediate flush. Single stop-token => apply pause-window. Also add a flag to disable pause-window for latency-sensitive customers.

jamie: LGTM. Can we also test memory impact of KV_TTL on large clusters? If too many pinned KV shards memory climbs.

noah: I'll measure memory delta. Preliminary looks like +2-4% mem under heavy-tool, acceptable but will quantify.

sarah: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread. If perf holds we'll promote to canary-wide next week. :rocket:
